report:
Non-contrast enhanced MR examination of right knee is performed with the pulse sequences - sagittal T1, PD+FS, and T2+FS, axial T2+FS and coronal T2+FS. And the imagings show : 

> Preserved joint space and alignment of right knee. 
> The continuity and alignment of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) are preserved without evidence of ligament tear. No evidence of tibial translation. Edematous soft tissue infiltration surrounding the ACL and PCL. Inflammation is favored. 
> Complex high signal intensities are identified in the posterior horn of medial meniscus. In favor of medial meniscus tear.
> Irregular high signal intensities are noted in the lateral meniscus. More in favor of disc degeneration. D/D include intrasubstance tear. 
> Presence of small to moderate  joint effusion.
> Continuity but increased signal intensity at the medial collateral ligament are noted. More in favor of grade I to II MCL strain. 
> No bone marrow edema. 
> Areas of increased signal intensity are noted in the lower portions of the quadriceps and patellar tendons. Tendinitis is considered. 
> Edematous soft tissue infiltration surrounding the knee. 
> The lateral collateral ligament, iliotibial tract,  cartilage, bone, and other structures are intact. 

<Impression> : 
1) In favor of medial meniscus tear in the posterior horn.
2) More in favor of disc degeneration in the lateral meniscus. D/D include intrasubstance tear. 
3) More in favor of grade I to II MCL strain. 
4) More in favor of tendinitis involving the portions of the quadriceps and patellar tendons.  
5) Presence of small to moderate  joint effusion.

Recommend clinical correlation and further evaluation.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    5 weeks ago patient felt popping sensation in the right knee during rotation motion. Able to weight-bear at the time of injury and presently tenderness at fibular head. Difficulty flexing the past 90 degrees. Ultrasound revealed effusion with synovial thickening and positive McMurray's test for medial aspect in clinic.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There are no normal intact fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament in keeping with a complete mid fiber tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The finding is associated with an anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment of about 8 mm. There is evidence of resolving bone contusions in the anterior lateral femoral condyle with slightly depressed anterior sulcus and resolving bone contusions in the posterior lateral tibial plateau. Findings are consistent with resolving kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is also edema in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau.

Buckling of the posterior cruciate ligament is noted in association with the anterior tibial drawer. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament is intact. There is some mild intrinsic signal around the deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament in keeping with a low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact including the fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, the popliteus tendon and the IT band.

There is an undisplaced vertical tear of the peripheral one third of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the posterior aspect of the posterior body. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment are well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is no significant Baker's cyst or significant knee effusion. There is mild reactive synovitis within the joint.

INTERPRETATION: 

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear of mid fibers associated with a significant anterior tibial drawer.

Resolving kissing bone contusions in association with pivot shift mechanism of injury.

Low-grade sprain of the medial fibers of medial collateral ligament.

Undisplaced radial tear of peripheral one third of posterior horn of medial meniscus extending into posterior body.

Moderate joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint in the lateral joint line.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss throughout the patella with areas of full-thickness loss at the median ridge and medial facet with associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Stripping of the prepatellar quadriceps continuation. Prepatellar bursitis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 12 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body, posterior horn and posterior root. Dominant complete radial component at the posterior root. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
2.	Mild-to-moderate tricompartmental osteoarthritis. Moderate knee joint effusion.
3.	Small leaking Baker's cyst.
4.	Prepatellar bursitis.
